trigger.details: Complexity Escalation threshold 'Regulatory surface area' (profiles/faa quality-risk-assessor methodology) triggers unconditionally — independent of cyclomatic complexity, coupling, or churn scores — whenever a module touches PII, financial calculations, or safety-critical paths. Direct source read plus Pass 1's independent decode of the committed studentDB.accdb confirm: (1) the 'students' table stores first/last name, father's name, two mobile numbers, and date of birth for named individuals; (2) the decode recovered real column values from data pages, confirming this is a live dataset, not an empty/seed schema; (3) zero authentication, authorization, or encryption exists anywhere in the application (AuthenticationMode=0, no login form across all 4 forms — Flat Design/My Project/Application.myapp:8); (4) a confirmed, exploitable SQL-injection vector (Flat Design/ViewForm.vb:50 — txtSearch.Text concatenated into both an equality clause and a LIKE clause) provides a live path to exfiltrate the entire dataset; (5) the repository is a public GitHub project per README.md and the hardcoded report URL at Flat Design/Form1.vb:156. Severity is set to 'critical' rather than the baseline 'standard/high' because this is an active, ongoing public exposure of real PII (not a latent or hypothetical risk) layered with a working injection vector and no access control of any kind — five of the application's six modules (module1-db-connection, form1-dashboard, insert-form, edit-form, view-form) read, write, or aggregate the affected table.

review_asks.title: Decide who owns remediation of the live student-PII exposure before this application proceeds past Discovery
review_asks.why: A stakeholder_required escalation that is approved past without a named resolver (or a documented reason to defer) makes the escalation type a label rather than a control, and leaves a real, exploitable PII exposure unaddressed.

confidence.rationale: Based on direct evidence: Pass 1's binary decode of studentDB.accdb recovered real column values (not schema alone), a full source read confirms zero authentication across all 4 forms, and the SQL-injection path at ViewForm.vb:50 was independently re-verified against the source in this pass.

review_asks.assessment: studentDB.accdb (784 KB), committed to what README.md and the embedded report URL identify as a public GitHub repository, contains live PII for named students — first/last name, father's name, two mobile numbers, and date of birth. The application that owns this data has no authentication, no authorization, and no encryption anywhere in its 461 hand-written lines, and ViewForm.vb:50 contains a confirmed, unparameterized SQL-injection path built from free-text search input that can read the entire table. This is an active data-governance incident rather than a design-time risk, and needs a named data-protection/privacy stakeholder (not an automated gate) to rule on remediation — e.g., purge the file from git history, restrict repository visibility, or confirm an accepted-risk disposition — before further modernization investment in this application.
review_asks.reasoning: Evidence is drawn from two independent passes: Pass 1 (legacy-architecture-mapper) decoded the Access ACE table-definition and data-page records directly from the binary .accdb and recovered real stored values, which rules out this being an empty template or seed-data fixture. This pass (quality-risk-assessor) independently re-read all 5 hand-written .vb files and confirmed no login form, no AuthenticationMode usage, and the exact unparameterized concatenation at ViewForm.vb:50. The two passes used different techniques (binary decode vs. source read) and reached the same conclusion, which is why confidence is high.

evidence_refs.name: PII recovered from binary decode
evidence_refs.detail: ACE table-definition and data-page decode of studentDB.accdb recovered real surname/gender values, confirming a live (not seed) PII dataset.

evidence_refs.name: No authentication anywhere in the application
evidence_refs.detail: AuthenticationMode=0 (Windows, unused), no login form in any of the 4 forms; every operator has unrestricted CRUD over all PII fields.

evidence_refs.name: Confirmed SQL-injection vector
evidence_refs.detail: txtSearch.Text concatenated directly into a SQL equality clause and a LIKE clause with no parameter binding; the only unsafe-input construction in the app that is exploitable today.

evidence_refs.name: Public repository context
evidence_refs.detail: README.md and a hardcoded Process.Start URL in Form1.vb:156 both point to a public github.com project page.

review_asks.title: For the record: this Discovery pass escalated one regulatory-surface finding (student PII exposure) for Student Management System (VB.NET)
review_asks.why: Documents that the quality-risk-assessor pass ran its mandatory escalation check and surfaced exactly one trigger, so the review record is explicit about what was checked rather than silent.

confidence.rationale: Derived directly from the methodology's unconditional 'regulatory surface area' rule applied against directly-observed source and data evidence; no inference beyond what both Discovery passes independently confirmed.

review_asks.assessment: One escalation (ESC-1) was recorded: five of six modules (module1-db-connection, form1-dashboard, insert-form, edit-form, view-form) touch the PII-bearing 'students' table, which mandates human review under the profile's complexity-escalation rubric regardless of this application's otherwise low cyclomatic complexity (max ≈4) and low afferent coupling (max fan-in 4, below the >8 threshold). No complexity- or coupling-threshold escalation was independently warranted; only the regulatory-surface rule fired.
